question: Distinguish memory-derived known-zero next-key dependency, predicted consumer control, and hardware prefetch effects in identical native instructions

factors.name: branch
factors.preparation: Canonical consumer predicted hit/miss branch with no-instruction side effect on hit

factors.name: constant
factors.preparation: Native independent zero materialization on absent completion; preserve all other semantics

factors.name: nops
factors.preparation: Exact inplace native ELF with PRFM replaced by same-width NOP; diagnostic only

measurement_limits: Initial three-repetition diagnostic; not the final seven-repetition panel
One immutable map per executable invocation; repeated operation preparation and all timed stage visits remain charged
Factor order alternates across different cases; a second optional pass reverses within each same case
Logical visits and potential hint targets are not PMU stalls, IPC or measured memory traffic
Original row-key layout; current owning-thread wider-value and key-layout changes excluded

Probe, layout, hint windows, request recurrence, jobs, and production Ring unchanged. NOP binary changes only PRFM instructions and reports exact byte receipt. Branch/constant are private causal controls.
